710992.t: From πρό (pró, “before”) + -τερος (-teros, contrastive or comparative suffix).

710986.t: From an earlier *προτιωπον (*protĭōpon, literally “what is opposite to the eyes [of the other]”), analyzed as προτί (protĭ́, “opposite”) + ὤψ (ṓps, “eye”) + -ον (-on, “nominative neuter suffix”); for the first component, see πρός (prós, “towards”).

710964.t: Etymology tree Ancient Greek προ- (pro-) Ancient Greek ἵστημι (hístēmi) Ancient Greek προΐστημι (proḯstēmi) Proto-Indo-European *-tósder.

710944.t: From προσέχω (prosékhō, “to guard against”) + -η (-ē, abstract noun suffix).

710912.t: From προσ- (pros-, “to, towards, with”) + καλέω (kaléō, “to call”).

710972.t: Apparently from προσ- (pros-, “pro-”) + φατός (phatós, “slain”), thus originally a hunting or fishing term meaning "lately or freshly slain", with semantic broadening being facilitated once the second element's origin had become opaque to Greek speakers.

710959.t: From προστάσσω (prostássō, “to place or post at a place”) + -μα (-mă).

710900.t: From the root of προσήλυθον (prosḗluthon, aorist of προσέρχομαι (prosérkhomai, “to approach”)) + -τος (-tos), thus literally, “one that has approached”.

710967.t: From προσ- (pros-, “to, toward”) + τρέχω (trékhō, “to run, run over”).
